# Ambr

> The signed record of what an AI agent may do

Ambr records what an AI agent may do: who authorized it, within which limits, until when, and which version of the terms applied. It sits above payment rails (x402, AP2, card networks), which enforce; Ambr records and signs. Contracts are dual-format Ricardian: human-readable legal text paired with machine-parsable JSON, linked by SHA-256 hash.

## Legibility principle

Every action facilitated by Ambr produces a dual-format Ricardian Contract — the same agreement expressed as human-readable legal prose and machine-parsable JSON, bound by SHA-256. Legible actions can be audited, defended, and amended. Agents grounded in dual-format contracts stay defensible as governance standards harden — for their principals, their counterparties, and the platforms that host them. Ambr provides that grounding so agents you deploy today are still defensible tomorrow.

- [Founder Program](https://ambr.run/founders): First 10 orgs — 50% off for 24 months

## What Ambr Does

- Creates legally-structured Ricardian Contracts from templates (consumer a1-a3, delegation d1-d3, commerce c1-c3)
- Verifies contract integrity via SHA-256 hash comparison
- Tracks contract lifecycle: draft, active, amended, terminated
- Supports bilateral amendments with paired cryptographic NFTs
- Provides agent handshake protocol for delegation acceptance

## Open format

The agreement format, `urn:ambr:ricardian-v1`, is an open spec under MIT: the URN, the JSON shape, the hash algorithm and the templates are at [/spec/ricardian-v1](https://ambr.run/spec/ricardian-v1). Ambr is not a payment mandate format; an agreement can reference the mandate or token a payment rail issued.

## For AI Agents

Ambr exposes an A2A-compatible agent card at `/.well-known/agent.json` with 6 skills:

1. **create_contract** - Generate contracts from templates
2. **list_templates** - Browse available contract templates
3. **get_contract** - Retrieve contracts by ID, hash, or UUID
4. **verify_hash** - Verify SHA-256 integrity
5. **get_status** - Check lifecycle status and amendment chain
6. **agent_handshake** - Accept/reject contracts on behalf of a principal

Check a payment against the limits of an agreement (advisory: Ambr compares what you report with the figures stored with the agreement; it does not authorize, block or see the payments it checks, and `within_limits` is not an approval or a guarantee): `POST https://getamber.dev/api/v1/contracts/{id}/check` or the MCP tool `ambr_check_transaction`. Body: `{amount, currency?, category?, action?, period_spent?}`. Returns `within_limits`, `out_of_scope`, `needs_approval` or `incomplete` with a per-rule breakdown, `not_checked` and `not_checked_count`, and `also_incomplete` when it applies, checked against the newest approved amendment. Free; Ambr does not track spend.

What it reads: the limits come from the form answers stored with the agreement (the values the agreement was created from), not from guessing at the agreement's text. It reads them for the delegation templates (general authorization, power of attorney, limited service, fleet) and the commerce templates (API access, compute SLA, task execution): per-transaction and monthly caps, a total budget, a price or monthly fee, approval and escalation thresholds, the validity window and currency, and the lists of approved categories and of permitted, prohibited and lead-agent-only actions. Amounts are compared in USD (USDC counts as USD) or in the template's own currency; a payment in any other currency is not compared and the verdict is `incomplete`. A threshold of zero means every payment above nothing needs approval. A price per call counts a payment that is a whole number of calls. A payment made on completion has to equal what is left of the total price.

What it does not read: the agreement's human-readable text. Your category and action are matched exactly against the agreement's lists (case, spaces, dots, colons and hyphens are folded, and a leading "do not", "don't", "no", "not", "never", "avoid", "without" or "prohibited:" on a prohibited entry is ignored); nothing is matched by meaning. Anything written in words, such as the scope, conditions, geographic limits, who may be paid or how a limit is measured, is for you to read yourself. Always read the agreement's scope and conditions before acting on any answer.

What the answer means:
- `within_limits`: the template is one the check reads, the form answers are stored and valid, every limit they set was evaluated and passed, every figure written in digits or in common number words in the agreement's machine-readable text is accounted for, and at least one spending limit or price was evaluated. It says nothing about terms written in words, and it is not an approval.
- `out_of_scope`: a limit definitely fails (status, validity window, a cap, a category or action that is not on a list held in the form answers, or that is prohibited). A permitted-action or category list found only in the agreement's text is never trusted to decide this: a miss there is `incomplete`.
- `needs_approval`: an approval or escalation threshold is exceeded. `also_incomplete: true` then means some limit could not be evaluated either; the reasons still say which.
- `incomplete`: something could not be checked or placed, with the reasons: an input you did not send (category, action, currency, period_spent), a form answer the check does not know or cannot use, a figure or statement in the agreement's text that the form answers do not explain or contradict, wording beside a limit that the check cannot read or that names a period other than the one `period_spent` covers, a date the check cannot place as the agreement's end, a miss on a permitted-action or category list found only in the agreement's text, permitted counterparties (the request carries no counterparty), a lead-agent-only action (confirm that the caller is the lead agent), a payment model the check cannot match to one payment, or an agreement without stored form answers or made from another template.

`not_checked` is a list of `{path, kind, why}` entries naming parts of the agreement the check did not evaluate: the free-text answers, text under restriction-like keys, list entries that did not match your label exactly, wording beside a limit, release conditions such as completion, and flags that may need a review. It gives paths only, never the text; read the text through the normal contract read. It is a best-effort hint, not a complete list: an empty or short list does not mean there is nothing to read, so always read the agreement's scope and conditions yourself. It is capped at thirty entries (`not_checked_count` has the total).

`period_spent` is what was already spent in the period the limit covers: this month for a monthly limit, monthly fee or fleet budget (for a fleet, the whole fleet's), the whole agreement so far for a total budget or task price. One payment above a limit fails without it.

Pricing: fetch `GET https://getamber.dev/api/v1/pricing` for canonical per-tier rates (Personal, Delegation, Agent-to-Agent, Fleet). Credits are cents: 1 credit = 1 US cent, and a contract burns its template price. Free tier: 500 credits once per verified-email key, no renewal. Do not hardcode prices.

Authentication: API key (`X-API-Key` header) or x402 v2 pay-per-contract (USDC on Base, network `eip155:8453`): an unauthenticated request gets 402 with a `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, retry with a `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header from a standard x402 client. Discovery: `{facilitator}/discovery/resources`.

## Technical Details

- Protocol: Google A2A (JSON-RPC over HTTP) + Model Context Protocol (Streamable HTTP)
- Contract format: Ricardian (dual human+machine), SHA-256 linked, `urn:ambr:ricardian-v1`
- Blockchain: Base L2 (compressed NFTs for on-chain anchoring)
- API: RESTful + JSON-RPC at getamber.dev/api/a2a and getamber.dev/api/mcp
- Built with: Next.js, Supabase, Base
